---
title: "Research"
---

My research examines how economies can respond to climate change while pursuing development, with a particular focus on **climate-compatible growth, climate policy, and applied microeconomics**.

## Climate-compatible growth

My doctoral research examines **green growth and climate-compatible development in lower- and middle-income countries**, with Nepal as the primary case study. I study how policy, markets, and institutions can support low-carbon economic transformation while accounting for development priorities, structural constraints, and labour-market outcomes.

*Current DPhil research · University of Oxford*

## Climate policy & technological transition

I study how policy and investment frameworks shape the development and deployment of emerging climate technologies. Before beginning my DPhil, I worked at [CO₂RE](https://co2re.org/) and the [Smith School of Enterprise and the Environment](https://www.smithschool.ox.ac.uk/) on the economics of greenhouse gas removal, including business-model viability, investment uncertainty, and policy design.

[View related publications →](publications.qmd)

## Environmental shocks & applied microeconomics

I use applied microeconomic approaches to study responses to environmental change and policy. My previous research includes work on **rainfall shocks and remittance inflows in Nepal** and experimental research on the adoption of energy-related technologies.

## Methods

Applied econometrics · Causal inference · R · Stata
